description:
Join us for #ProudandFree: United for Trans Power this Saturday

WHEN: Saturday, June 21st, 1:00 - 3:00pm 

WHERE: Boise, Idaho (exact location given after registration)

On Wednesday, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a devastating decision in U.S. v. Skrmetti, ruling to block access to potentially life-saving medical care that allows trans people to live their lives as they see fit.

U.S. v. Skrmetti is a lawsuit filed by the ACLU, Lambda Legal, the ACLU of Tennessee, and Akin Gump on behalf of transgender youth and their families challenging Tennessee’s categorical ban (SB1) on gender-affirming medical care for transgender youth.

The Court’s ruling against trans youth, their families, and their doctors threatens the well-being of trans people, the safety of our communities, and the ability of every family to determine what is best for them. It is an attack on the right of each of us to control our own future.

In Idaho and across the United States, we will gather in community to say that we believe our freedom to be ourselves is worth fighting for. No matter what the challenges, we will always be proud and free.

Join us this Saturday, June 21 from 1:00-3:00 pm in Boise, Idaho as we unite in solidarity for trans freedom, joy, and power with activists across the country organized by the ACLU and Lambda Legal. Help us to take on bullies, build trans power, and do our part so that trans youth grow up to be happy, healthy trans adults. Learn more about the harmful decision and it's implications for Idaho, be in community, and get resources to navigate the fight ahead. 

No matter what the Court or politicians say, transgender youth and their families are not alone. We will continue to fight in courtrooms and communities across the country to ensure all people have the freedom to shape their own futures.

This event is hosted by the ACLU of Idaho in partnership with Trans Joy Boise, Mama Dragons, and Planned Parenthood Pacific Pride Foundation, PFLAG Santa Barbara, and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates - Idaho

title: Bigger Than Dobbs II: Stop Trump's War on Women
description:
Bigger Than Dobbs II: Stop Trump's and the GOP's War on Women

March Forward/Indivisible Quincy is organizing a "Bigger Than Dobbs'' rally to Stop the War on Women, Sunday 6/29 from 2-4 pm in the Hancock Adams Common outside Quincy City Hall. Speakers will include local activists, organizations, and elected officials. Some signs will be provided, but feel free to bring your own!

Our event is part of a weekend of action supported by Indivisible and the Women's March to mark the anniversary of the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision, sadly overturning the decades of case law for Roe vs Wade. In the barrage of attacks on our democracy, it is marginalized groups and women who are the targets. Despite our warnings and protests, the current Republican party, with Donald Trump at the helm, have accelerated their plan to implement Project 2025.

Their plan to restore a white, Christian patriarchy was clearly stated in Project 2025. We warned that Republicans were "turning back the clock" and that "abortion was just the tip of the iceberg."  Each section detailed how the freedoms of women would be curtailed. As we pointed out, abortion bans are just the beginning. Their aim is to put women back into traditional "Biblically-based marriages," without careers or reproductive rights or even the right to vote, and to punish those who won't abide by their rules. 

In the time since SCOTUS ruled to overturn Roe, we have seen a degradation of democracy across the board while attacks on women have been quietly happening. There aren't armed, masked men abducting women who won't comply (yet) but it’s clear - from the cancellation of medical research pertaining to women, to the firings of top female military officials, to voter suppression law specifically targeting married women, the GOP War on Women must be stopped. This is our message: Stop Trump's War on Women!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action | Desaparecidos en los Estados Unidos (Freehold - Address TBD)
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** 
Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

**NOTE: Exact location TBD.** Watch this space for more details to be posted shortly.

🚨 **On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.** 🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this event is to encourage attendees to call their congress members and Senators to VOTE NO on Budget Reconciliation bill. This bill will funnel $150 billion into ICE’s brutal enforcement machine, fueling mass raids, indefinite child detention, and violent deportations. It rips away protections for unaccompanied children, forcing them into dangerous examinations, detention centers, and trafficking risks. This proposal will impose a cruel $1,000 fee for asylum seekers – putting a clear price on safety, a price on survival. We REFUSE to stand by while our communities live in terror! Every day, ICE arrests 2,000 people — parents torn from their children, workers stolen from their jobs, families shattered in an instant. This budget enables state-sanctioned brutality, turning neighborhoods into hunting grounds, homes into war zones, and streets into traps. Let’s be clear: this is tyranny. This is an assault on human dignity. This budget bill must be STOPPED.

Another key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions. Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._


**En los Estados Unidos, el gobierno no tiene el derecho de raptar a las personas de las calles, saltarse el proceso judicial y enviarlas directamente a una prisión extranjera.** "Desaparecidos en los Estados Unidos de América" es un día de acción nacional para defender el estado de derecho y denunciar los secuestros, detenciones y deportaciones ilegales llevadas a cabo por la administración de Trump contra personas como Kilmar Abrego García, Rui Marras y Juan Maldonado Zúñiga. 

**NOTA: Ubicación exacta por determinar.** Esté atento a este espacio para obtener más detalles que se publicarán en breve.

🚨**El jueves 26 de junio, nos reuniremos en los tribunales y plazas de todo el país para decir: en Estados Unidos, no permitimos que el gobierno desaparezca personas. Eso no es lo que somos.**🚨 

Creemos en el estado de derecho, y los tribunales han dictaminado que el debido proceso es obligatorio. Si un presidente puede ignorar los tribunales y hacer desaparecer a residentes legales, no hay límite para lo que vendrá después. Trump ha declarado que quiere secuestrar y deportar ciudadanos estadounidenses. Si esto no se detiene ahora, nadie estará seguro.

**Día Nacional de Petición Fotográfica - 26 de Junio En este día, llenaremos las redes sociales con la verdad, tomando fotografías con carteles de quienes han sido desaparecidos y exigiendo justicia.

**Exigimos un VOTO NO sobre la Reconciliación Presupuestaria
Este proyecto de ley destinaría $150 mil millones a la brutal máquina de deportación de ICE, alimentando redadas masivas, detención indefinida de niños y deportaciones violentas. Eliminaría protecciones para niños no acompañados, sometiéndolos a exámenes invasivos, detención y riesgos de tráfico humano. Además, impondría un cruel pago de $1,000 para quienes buscan asilo—poniendo un precio a la seguridad, un precio a la supervivencia.

No podemos quedarnos de brazos cruzados mientras nuestras comunidades viven con terror. Cada día, ICE arresta a 2,000 personas—padres arrancados de sus hijos, trabajadores desaparecidos de sus empleos, familias destruidas en un instante. Este presupuesto financia brutalidad estatal, convirtiendo vecindarios en campos de caza, hogares en zonas de guerra y calles en trampas**.

Esto es tiranía. Esto es un ataque a la dignidad humana. Este proyecto de presupuesto debe ser BLOQUEADO.

Responsabilidad de los Sheriffs: No colaboren con ICE
Otro objetivo de esta campaña es exigir a los sheriffs locales que se nieguen a cooperar con las órdenes de ICE para participar en redadas, transferencias a centros de detención, y alquiler de camas en cárceles para ICE. Los sheriffs tienen amplia discreción sobre su nivel de cooperación, y su participación en estas prácticas solo erosiona la confianza de la comunidad en las autoridades locales.

_Un principio fundamental de todos los eventos de Desaparecidos en América es el compromiso con la acción no violenta. Esperamos que todos los participantes busquen reducir la tensión ante cualquier posible confrontación con quienes discrepan de nuestros valores._

title: Bethel Defends Democracy: Whose Country? OUR Country!
description:
Please join us for our 16th consecutive rally to Defend Democracy in beautiful downtown Bethel. While our overall theme is Defending Democracy, each week we pick a specific focus. On Saturday June 21st, 11am - noon,  back at PT Barnum Square, our focus is to bask in the success of our No Kings rally:
Whose Country? OUR Country!

We are said NO to authoritarianism. 
We are said NO to fascism. 
We are said NO to a dictatorship. 

We are sharing the square this week with our town's Music in the Park event which will start on our square at 12:30pm.  Their event is weather permitting but we are rain or shine or unbearable humidity (good thing we have some lovely large trees for shade).  So come rally for a while, enjoy lunch in town and then some music in the park!

We'll rally with our signs and take a short march. We also like to end each week with a sing-a-long.

The rally is non-partisan. What this means is that like-minded people from diverse backgrounds are participating and are vital to our rallies. Defending Democracy crosses party lines: we have registered Republicans, Unaffiliated, Democrats, and non-voters, all coming together to fight for the rights of “We the People” to determine the type of society we want to live in.

A sign-making table will also be available, complete with all the necessary supplies, for young and old to make signs for the rally.

We also collect a non-perishable food item for our local food pantry each week. The food pantry greatly appreciates the donations each week!  Anything you want to contribute is welcome, but some special requests from the food pantry include:

sunscreen

bug spray

Neither can be bought with SNAP but are vital for folks working outdoors in the summer or for kids who will be attending outdoor camps while school is out. Smaller containers that would fit inside a lunchbox are ideal size!

 We are currently lowest on baking supplies, pudding, and jello. Pudding and jello can either be the box mix or predone cups. 

Spices, Coffee and Baking supplies are always needed.

Individually packaged items. If you bought a variety pack of something like granola bars or instant oatmeal and discovered there's a flavor you won't eat, please give us the individual packs out of box.

Empty egg cartons- Any style, so long as they're clean.

SMALL empty detergent bottles

Note: Rally is rain or shine.

We ask that attendees refrain from sign holding or chanting at the curb during our speaking portion of the rally. We have had issues with speakers being heard because of the increased honking. It also is a courtesy to the speakers who are often discussing serious and sensitive topics. We are sharing a small square so we need your help to make the rallies comfortable for everyone.

We have tried to arrange the rallies so there is a little something for everyone: chanting, marching, themes with speakers, live music, fun trinkets, sign making. We appreciate every one of you that attends and we are working hard to bring all of us together to voice our frustrations, build community and also hopefully learn a little something from experts or your fellow neighbors experiences.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation. ❤️

We also ask that you park at one of the four public parking lots. The lots that are the closest to the rally location, the Municipal Center, are the lot behind the municipal center and the train station lot on Durant Ave.

Although all street parking is public, we ask that you please not park in the limited parking spots in front of our local businesses, but definitely enjoy our beautiful towns restaurants and shops after the rally! 
Thank you 😊

title: Civil Rights Movement Lessons for Democratic Organizing - Democracy Action Network / Indivisible
description:
The civil rights movement created the most successful example of democracy as a way of life in American history, building beloved community that sustained people through brutal repression while achieving transformational political victories, and this session teaches you the practical skills they developed for conflict transformation, consensus building, and democratic education that you can apply immediately to your current organizing work.


We want everyone to read the book, ["Waging a Good War
A Military History of the Civil Rights Movement, 1954-1968," by Thomas E. Ricks.](https://us.macmillan.com/books/9780374605162/wagingagoodwar/)

In Waging a Good War, the bestselling author Thomas E. Ricks offers a fresh perspective on America’s greatest moral revolution—the civil rights movement of the 1950s and 1960s—and its legacy today. While the Movement has become synonymous with Martin Luther King, Jr.’s ethos of nonviolence, Ricks, a Pulitzer Prize–winning war reporter, draws on his deep knowledge of tactics and strategy to advance a surprising but revelatory idea: the greatest victories for Black Americans of the past century were won not by idealism alone, but by paying attention to recruiting, training, discipline, and organization—the hallmarks of any successful military campaign.

Building on the culture-first organizing frameworks from Session 1, you'll study 
- How Septima Clark's citizenship schools turned democratic education into community organizing infrastructure, 
- How SNCC developed participatory democracy and consensus decision-making under extreme pressure, 
- How mass meetings and freedom songs created the cultural foundation for sustained resistance, and 
- How the movement combined personal transformation, alternative institution building, and institutional change into an integrated strategy that changed what Americans believed was possible. 

Through hands-on practice with civil rights organizing methods, you'll develop concrete skills for building democratic culture that meets people's immediate needs while creating the infrastructure for long-term political transformation, leaving equipped with time-tested tools for the historic democracy organizing work that lies ahead.

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

Join LGBTQIA+ folks and advocates for Community Circle gatherings in Reno and Las Vegas!

The Supreme Court has failed to protect families' freedoms and allowed politicians' targeting of transgender youth's healthcare needs to stand.
